subject: DELETE statement
notes: This is genuine implementor latitude -- the standard requires the implementor to DEFINE which fixed-file attributes DELETE FILE validates (9.1.6), and Annex F item 50 makes the definition mandatory and mandatorily documented: '50) DELETE FILE statement (validation of fixed file attributes). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.10, DELETE statement, General rule 19)'. What exists today: FileRegistry.DeleteFile validates NO attributes (see GR18), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md lines 103-105 document that as 'Documented non-support until a physical-attribute store exists'. Those are two different claims and the difference is exactly what needs deciding. An EMPTY validated set is a legally-definable implementor choice (the standard nowhere requires the set to be non-empty), in which case the fix is a one-line documented implementor definition in CONFORMANCE.md phrased as the Annex-required item and GR18 becomes vacuously satisfied; a NON-EMPTY set requires building the fixed-attribute store GR18 needs. The bare owner question: is WiseOwl COBOL's validated fixed-file-attribute set for DELETE FILE (and, per 14.9.27.4 GR10, for OPEN) empty by design and to be documented as such, or is the attribute store to be built? I am not permitted to choose documented non-support (owner decision D13), and the current wording is a deferral rather than a definition, so the row cannot be closed by an adjudicator. || UPHELD as NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION, with a CITATION CORRECTION and one substantive amendment. CITATION: 'Annex F item 50' names the WRONG ANNEX -- Annex F in this standard is 'Archaic and obsolete language element lists' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 44027). The item lives in Annex A.1, the Implementor-defined language element list, and I validated it mechanically: 'python scripts/spec/cite.py --check A.1 \"DELETE FILE statement (validation of fixed file attributes). This item is required.\"' returns 'OK A.1 50) (Implementor-defined language element list)' with the full text '50) DELETE FILE statement (validation of fixed file attributes). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.10, DELETE statement, General rule 19)'. This is precisely the inherited-citation failure mode -- the quoted text was genuinely in the standard and the annex letter was never re-derived -- so the corrected reference is A.1 item 50 wherever this propagates into code comments, CONFORMANCE.md or the DEVLOG. SUBSTANCE: I confirm docs/CONFORMANCE.md:103-105 is a DEFERRAL ('Documented non-support until a physical-attribute store exists'), not the A.1-item-50 definition GR19 demands, and that ground rule 6 / owner decision D13 forbid an adjudicator from converting one into the other. The bare question is correctly framed. AMENDMENT for whoever answers it: an EMPTY set closes THIS row but does NOT close GR-14.9.10.4-18, whose OVERRIDE-phrase half is a grammar gap independent of the attribute store -- see that row's refinement. || OWNER DETERMINATION RECORDED 2026-08-31 (owner protocol 2026-08-30 + a survey unanimous among the implementations that HAVE the statement); NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION -> CONFORMS. THE BARE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED IS ANSWERED: WiseOwl COBOL's validated fixed-file-attribute set for DELETE FILE is EMPTY BY DESIGN and is now documented as such. THAT SATISFIES THE RULE RATHER THAN WAIVING IT: cite.py --check 14.9.10.4 'The implementor shall define which of the fixed-file attributes are validated during the execution of the DELETE FILE statement' -> OK (GR19). The obligation is to DEFINE the set; the rule nowhere requires it to be non-empty, so an empty definition discharges GR19 exactly as a non-empty one would. GR19's second sentence permits the set to vary by organization or storage medium - ours does NOT vary, which is stated explicitly because 'uniformly empty' is a stronger and simpler thing to rely on than 'empty for the cases we tried'. THE CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NEVER RE-DERIVED AS A DEFECT: GR18 sets '39' when the connector's attributes and the physical file's fixed attributes do not match, so with nothing validated there is nothing to mismatch and '39' is UNREACHABLE FROM DELETE FILE BY DEFINITION, not by omission. DOCUMENTED where the standard asks: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 now carries the Annex A.1 item-50 determination row (cite.py --check A.1 'DELETE FILE statement (validation of fixed file attributes). This item is required.' -> OK A.1 50), and audit_annex_a1.py counts item 50 discharged (164 -> 163 remaining obligations). The §3 '39' bullet's DEFERRAL wording ('documented non-support until a physical-attribute store exists') is REPLACED - a deferral is not a definition, which is precisely what the prior adjudicator and refuter both said blocked this row. TEST: 2023/delete_file_attribute_set_empty issues a DELETE FILE through a connector contradicting the physical file in TWO of the attributes §9.1.6 names as fixed (the organization - 'the primary attribute' - and the logical record size, 20 vs 40 bytes) and requires it to delete with GR20 a)'s '00'; the deletion is then shown to be real (GR14's successful '05' on the re-delete, §9.1.13.4's '35' on OPEN INPUT). The golden was proven to DISCRIMINATE before it was trusted: with '39' substituted for the expected '00' the corpus runner goes red on that case by name. THE OPEN SIBLING IS SPLIT OFF, NOT SWEPT IN: §14.9.27.4 GR10 / A.1 item 129 (OPEN's validated set) is a SEPARATE required obligation whose set is NOT empty on the same survey - it needs the persisted physical-attribute catalog - and is now kb/Work PB193. GR-14.9.10.4-18 is likewise untouched: its OVERRIDE-phrase half is a grammar gap independent of the attribute store (kb/Work PB196).
